title: On-call and Incident Response Playbook: Standards, Runbooks, and Templates (2026)
author: Alexandra Kim
content:
Overview:

This playbook centralizes Redwood Inference's standards, runbook templates, postmortem expectations, on-call rotation rules, game day guidance, and customer/status-page communications templates. It is intended for on-call engineers, incident commanders (ICs), SRE, and engineering managers. Follow the procedures below for all Sev2/Sev1 incidents; treat lower severity incidents according to team runbooks.

Goals:
- Restore service quickly and safely.
- Communicate internally and externally with clarity and timeliness.
- Capture actionable learnings and reduce recurrence.

Scope:
- Applies to all production-facing Redwood services (hosted API, Dedicated control plane, Private deployment control plane, runtime clusters).
- Non-production incidents (staging/dev) should follow the same playbook scaled to impact.

1) Incident Severity Definitions:

- Sev1 (Critical): Extensive service outage or data loss affecting the majority of customers or critical business flows. Target P1 MTTR: 1 hour. Requires immediate paging of on-call and escalation to engineering leadership.
- Sev2 (High): Major degradation impacting a subset of customers or important latencies/throughput regressions. Target P2 MTTR: 4 hours. Requires on-call response and IC.
- Sev3 (Medium): Partial loss or non-critical functionality. Handled by on-call with follow-ups in business hours.
- Sev4 (Low): Informational or minor issues; triaged during normal cycles.

2) Incident Lifecycle (Step-by-step):

- Detection and Triage:
  1. Pager triggers or alerts via PagerDuty/Prometheus/CloudWatch/Datadog.
  2. On-call acknowledges within defined SLA (Sev1: 5 minutes, Sev2: 15 minutes).
  3. On-call posts an incident thread in #incidents Slack channel and creates a dedicated channel named incident-<service>-YYYYMMDD-HHMM (e.g., incident-runtime-20260210-0915).
  4. Quick triage: confirm impact, affected customers/regions, and severity.

- Assign Incident Commander (IC):
  1. If on-call is the senior engineer on the pager, they become IC by default for first 30 minutes.
  2. If escalation needed, IC handoff occurs with a one-line summary, current hypothesis, and outstanding actions.
  3. IC responsibilities: coordinate mitigation, call for runbook owners, maintain timeline, and sign off on external comms.

- Mitigation and Recovery:
  1. Follow the relevant runbook (see Runbooks section).
  2. If no runbook exists or the runbook is insufficient, IC initiates ad-hoc troubleshooting and documents hypotheses and experiments in the incident channel.
  3. Prioritize restoring customer-facing functionality first; use fallbacks (e.g., route to compatible model variant, throttle non-critical workloads).
  4. Track actions in the incident timeline table (below).

- Post-incident Actions:
  1. When service is restored and stable for 2x verification window, IC declares incident resolved and documents final timeline.
  2. IC opens a postmortem ticket in the incident backlog and assigns an author. Postmortem must be created within 5 business days for Sev1/Sev2.
  3. Apply immediate fixes as remediation tasks and track in engineering backlog with severity and owner.

3) Runbooks (Structure and Required Fields):

Every production runbook must include the following top-level fields and be stored in the team runbooks directory:
- Service name
- Owner and secondary owner (name + pager)
- Runbook last_updated date
- Preconditions and SLOs impacted (e.g., API p99 latency > 600ms, error rate > 1%)
- Detection signals and authoritative dashboards
- Step-by-step mitigation steps (numbered)
- Rollback procedures and safe roll-forward rules
- Post-incident checklist and cleanup steps

Sample runbook header (markdown):

"""
Service: runtime-gateway
Owner: eng-runtime (oncall: alice.nguyen@redwood.com, pager: +1-555-0100)
Secondary: eng-infra (sre-oncall@redwood.com)
Last updated: 2026-01-18
SLOs affected: request-success-rate >= 99.9% over 10m window, p99 latency < 500ms
"""

Example step sequence:
1) Validate the alert: check Datadog monitor, API Gateway logs, and recent deploys.
2) If spike correlates with new deploy, run: `kubectl rollout history deploy/runtime-gateway -n prod` and read last deploy ID.
3) If deploy suspected, rollback: `kubectl rollout undo deploy/runtime-gateway -n prod --to-revision=<previous>` and monitor p99 for 10 minutes.
4) If CPU/GPU saturation: check autoscaler logs and scale group quotas, run `aws autoscaling describe-auto-scaling-groups --query 'AutoScalingGroups[*].[AutoScalingGroupName,DesiredCapacity]'`

4) Escalation Matrix and Contact List:

- Primary on-call (team-level) -> Secondary on-call -> Team lead -> SRE manager -> Eng Director -> CTO for Sev1 persistent > 4 hours.
- Use PagerDuty escalation policy "prod-sev1" for immediate pages.

Contact table (example):
Service owner: eng-runtime@redwood.com
Pager contacts: Primary oncall pager (see PagerDuty)
SRE manager: Marcus Patel (marcus.patel@redwood.com)
Security on-call: sec-oncall@redwood.com
Customer Success escalation: customer-success@redwood.com

5) Incident Timeline Template (copy into incident channel):

- Incident start: 2026-02-10 09:12 UTC
- Detection signal: Datadog monitor `runtime-latency-p99` triggered at 09:11:58
- Initial impact: p99 latency increased to 820ms; error rate 2.4%
- Actions taken:
  - 09:13: Acknowledged and created incident channel
  - 09:16: IC assigned (Alice Nguyen)
  - 09:20: Rolled back latest runtime-gateway deploy (revision 2015)
  - 09:30: Metrics returned to p99 480ms. Confirming stability.
- Resolution declared: 09:40 UTC

6) Postmortem Template and Expectations:

Every Sev1/Sev2 incident must produce a postmortem with the following sections:
- Title (short descriptive)
- Incident summary (one-paragraph)
- Timeline (annotated)
- Impact (customers affected, duration, data loss)
- Root cause analysis (findings, contributing factors)
- Corrective actions (short-term hotfixes and long-term preventative tasks)
- Owners and due dates for actions
- Follow-up (link to related PRs, config changes, runbook updates)
- Severity classification and lessons learned

Postmortem style rules:
- Avoid blame; focus on facts.
- Include logs/graphs links and relevant runbook snippets.
- Author must propose at least two preventive actions for Sev1 incidents.
- Completion SLA: draft within 5 business days; final review and publish within 10 business days.

7) On-call Rotations and Responsibilities:

Rotation rules:
- Primary on-call rotates weekly for SRE/infra teams; product/feature teams may use 1-week or 2-week rotations depending on team norms.
- Each rotation must have a documented secondary (cross-team backup) and an escalation contact.
- Engineers on-call must maintain a minimum 2-week notice before PTO and arrange a swap in PagerDuty.

On-call responsibilities:
- Acknowledge pages within SLA and follow triage process.
- Keep the incident channel updated every 15 minutes for Sev1 and every 30 minutes for Sev2 during active mitigation.
- Perform a short handoff note at the start and end of shift in the team on-call doc.

Handoff checklist (short):
- Current open alerts and mitigation state
- Active incidents and assignees
- Recent deploys and config changes
- Known flaky signals to ignore

8) Game Day Guidance (quarterly):

Purpose: validate operational runbooks, improve coordination, and test runbook accuracy under load.

Game day cadence and ownership:
- Quarterly enterprise-wide game day hosted by Eng SRE with participation from Runtime, Infra, and Customer Success.
- Game day owner: SRE manager (Marcus Patel).

Game day structure (example half-day):
1) Pre-brief (15m): goals, systems in scope, non-goal list.
2) Injects (2-3): e.g., simulated region outage, model serving degradation, auth service latency.
3) Live response (60-90m): teams operate in incident mode; ICs rotate.
4) Debrief (30m): capture gaps, update runbooks, assign follow-up actions.

Post-game day requirements:
- Game day report published to the incident channel and the team runbooks page within 3 business days.
- Update any runbooks that failed to guide responders.

9) Status Page and Customer Communications Templates:

Status page incident lifecycle messages (short templates):
- Initial (within 30 minutes of detection for Sev1/Sev2):
  Title: "Partial outage impacting runtime API - Investigating"
  Body: "We are currently investigating increased latency and errors impacting the runtime API in us-west-2. Customers may see elevated latencies or failed requests. Our engineers are actively diagnosing the issue. We will post updates every 30 minutes or as new information is available."
- Update (example):
  Title: "Mitigation in progress - rolling back recent deploys"
  Body: "We have identified a likely regression in the runtime-gateway deploy and are rolling back the change. We expect partial recovery within 30 minutes. We will post another update at 10:00 UTC or earlier if the situation changes."
- Resolved: 
  Title: "Incident resolved - runtime API"
  Body: "The issue has been resolved and services are operating normally. We will publish a postmortem with root cause and actions within 5 business days. We apologize for the impact."

Customer e-mail template (for high-impact incidents):
Subject: "Service Incident Update: Runtime API - [status]"
Body:
Hello {customer_name},

We are writing to let you know about an incident that affected the Runtime API on {date}.
- What happened: short summary of impact.
- What we did: immediate mitigation and timeline.
- Current status: resolved / mitigated / ongoing.
- Next steps: link to postmortem and follow-up actions.

We apologize for the disruption. If you have questions, contact your account team or support at support@redwood.com.

10) Communication Best Practices:

- Use plain language; avoid engineering jargon in customer-facing messages.
- Be transparent about impact and timelines.
- Do not speculate publicly about root cause until confirmed.
- Coordinate with Legal/PR for incidents with data loss or regulatory impact.

11) Metrics and SLO Impact Tracking:

- Track the following during and after incidents: p99 latency, error rate, request volume, CPU/GPU utilization, autoscaler events.
- Add post-incident SLO impact calculation: lost availability in customer minutes (total customers * downtime minutes) and alerting false positives.

12) Templates and Checklist (copyable items):

- Incident channel creation command (Slack): `/incident create runtime-gateway "Sev1 latency spike"`
- Incident start snippet (paste to channel):
  "Incident kickoff - Service: runtime-gateway | Severity: Sev1 | IC: @alice.nguyen | Summary: p99 latency spike to 820ms"
- Postmortem checklist (checkbox list):
  - [ ] Create postmortem ticket
  - [ ] Author draft (5 business days)
  - [ ] Assign action owners with due dates
  - [ ] Review with leadership
  - [ ] Publish and link to runbook updates

13) Ownership and Governance:

- Runbook ownership: team that owns the service. On-call rotation owners must review runbook at the start of each rotation.
- Playbook governance: Eng SRE maintains this playbook; changes must be reviewed by SRE manager and one engineering manager.

Appendix A: Troubleshooting Commands and Dashboards (examples)
- Datadog monitors: https://app.datadoghq.com/monitors/runtime-latency-p99
- Kubernetes: `kubectl get pods -n prod -l app=runtime-gateway -o wide`
- Autoscaling: `aws autoscaling describe-auto-scaling-groups --auto-scaling-group-names runtime-gpu-pool`
- Logs: `aws logs tail /aws/lambda/runtime-handler --since 1h`

Appendix B: Quick reference — Who to page
- PagerDuty policy: prod-sev1 -> oncall -> secondary -> eng-lead -> sre-manager.
- Security incident: page sec-oncall and file incident in Security tracker.

Appendix C: Example Postmortem Link (public internal formatting)
Title: "Postmortem: runtime-gateway latency spike (2026-02-10)"
Summary: Short one-paragraph.
Timeline: table (time, actor, action, notes).
Root cause: deploy with untested kernel selection that increased p99 under long sequences.
Actions: rollback quick-fail, add pre-deploy perf test, update runbook.

Notes:
- This playbook is a living document. Submit changes via PR to the eng-sre docs repo and tag @Marcus Patel for review.
- For legal or regulatory escalation, contact legal@redwood.com and Security on-call immediately.
